root_cause.text: Using devm_register_netdev() defers unregister_netdev() to the devres cleanup phase after emac_remove() tears down hardware, allowing the network stack to access freed hardware resources (e.g., dev->emacp, dev->mal) during packet processing.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces devm_register_netdev() with manual register_netdev() and moves unregister_netdev() to the beginning of emac_remove() before any hardware teardown, as described in the commit message: "unregister_netdev() at the beginning of emac_remove(), before any hardware teardown. This ensures the network device is fully stopped and unregistered before hardware resources are released." The commit also states: "devm_register_netdev() which causes unregister_netdev() to be deferred until the devres cleanup phase, which runs after emac_remove() returns. This creates a use-after-free window."

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix net device registration by switching from managed to unmanaged API to avoid devres-related issues.
intent_record.what: Replaced devm_register_netdev(&ofdev->dev, ndev) with register_netdev(ndev) in emac_probe function.
intent_record.how: The network device registration is no longer managed by the device resource management (devres) framework, requiring explicit unregistration in error paths or remove callback.

intent_record.intent_summary: Reorder teardown in emac_remove to unregister the net device before cancelling work, preventing a use-after-free race condition.
intent_record.what: Added a call to unregister_netdev(dev->ndev) before cancel_work_sync(&dev->reset_work) in the emac_remove function, along with a comment explaining the rationale.
intent_record.how: This change reorders the teardown sequence so that the network device is unregistered from the network stack before pending work (reset_work) is canceled and hardware resources are released, preventing the stack from accessing the net_device after its resources are freed.
